tokens.source: transcript message.usage summed across 916 usage-bearing assistant records in <home>/.claude/projects/<repo-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl (cached_input = cache_read + cache_creation; uncached_input = input_tokens; total_input = their sum; 412055 of the output tokens were thinking tokens). Covers the whole session, which spans PRs 12 through 15, not this deliverable alone -- usage attaches per model turn, so it cannot be split per deliverable. retries, setup_overhead and tool_overhead have no source on this runtime and are recorded as unknown, never zero.

unproven: Command tails and sha256 values are SANITIZED, not verbatim: absolute paths become <repo> and <home> before hashing.
'commit' names 229bd309, the substantive head, not the squash-merge commit GitHub creates at merge time. The directive-7 gates key on 'pr' for that reason.

The env-leak scan's needles come from LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES in this session's environment. The independent reviewer could NOT confirm that result -- its own environment has no needles configured and it was instructed not to guess private-name values -- so the clean scan is the author's claim, checked only by CI's own run against the repository secret.
The token figures cover the entire session across PRs 12-15. No mechanism attributes tokens to one deliverable, one PR or one tool call, because usage attaches per model turn.
The commit-msg hook is not installed by cloning. It protects only a checkout where `git config core.hooksPath scripts/githooks` has been run; CI's lwb-lanes job remains the backstop.

reviewer_id and commit_author_id are self-attested strings. Nothing cross-checks them against git authorship or a session registry, so reviews/15/ is an audit trail, not proof that two independent sessions existed.
This record was written by the author of the work it proves. 'checked_by' names the independent reviewer of the code, not an independent checker of this record's own contents.
